name: SFTP
description: A two-pane SFTP client for your own servers, like FileZilla. Connect with a host, username, password and port — or an SSH key — then browse this device and the server side by side and drag files across. Every connection goes straight from this device to your server; nothing passes through a luma server. A Nova-exclusive plugin.
details:
Add your servers to the Site Manager with the details you already know: host name or IP, username, password and port. Prefer keys? Point luma at an OpenSSH or PEM private key instead and it will ask for the passphrase if the key has one. Passwords and passphrases are only remembered when you tick the box, and when you do they are encrypted on this device with a key that never leaves it.

Once connected you get the two-pane layout a transfer client is meant to have: this device on the left, the server on the right, both with breadcrumbs, an up button and a folder listing showing size, date and POSIX permissions. Drag files or folders from one side to the other, or select them and use the transfer arrows. Whole folders transfer recursively, and the queue below shows every file with its own progress bar and speed, running two at a time. Stop anything mid-flight, or put a failed transfer back on the queue with one tap.

Right-click (or long-press on a phone) for the rest: rename, delete, make a new folder, change permissions on the server with 755 or rwxr-xr-x notation, or open a local file in whatever app normally handles it. On a phone the two panes become tabs, with the queue as a third.

The first time you connect to a server, luma shows you its SSH fingerprint and asks whether to trust it — and refuses to connect silently if that key ever changes, the way a proper SSH client should. Nothing about any of this involves a luma account or a luma server: the SSH socket is opened by this device, straight to the address you typed.

SFTP is included free with the Nova plan.
